title: KoreLumina — Master OS - KoreLumina Platform Handoff — message 4

metadata.content:
That is the one major piece missing from the handoff. Without it, a new conversation could start implementing KP as if it has no history, which defeats one of its core purposes.
I'd add a dedicated section immediately after the KP section.
Repository Knowledge Seeding (Mandatory Before KP Development)PurposeKP must never begin with an empty knowledge base.Before implementing new capabilities, KoreLumina must recover, normalize, and ingest knowledge that already exists in the repository.The repository is the first engineer.KP learns from the repository before it learns from future implementations.Knowledge SourcesKnowledge is seeded from the following sources, in order of priority.1. Architecture DocumentsLocated under:docs/architecture/These define:platform architectureengineering principlescapability boundariesruntime contractspublic vs internal capabilitiesproduction workflowgovernanceroadmapspecificationsArchitecture documents are authoritative.2. Git HistoryKP must analyze repository history.Recover:completed featuresimplementation patternsarchitectural evolutionregression fixesproduction fixesengineering decisionsEvery meaningful commit is potential engineering knowledge.3. Existing ImplementationCurrent source code represents implemented engineering decisions.Recover knowledge from:RuntimeBuilderAIDeploymentRepository IntelligenceInfrastructureExtract:capabilitiesinterfacesdependency graphsworkflowsinvariants4. Historical ReconstructionsRecover knowledge from:reconciliation documentsADRsRFCsimplementation trackersroadmap documentsarchived architectural documentsThese preserve why previous engineering decisions were made.5. Landing ContractThe landing page defines public promises.KP must understand:customer expectationsproduct boundariespublic capabilitiesenterprise capabilitiesImplementation must never contradict these promises.6. Previous LessonsRecover lessons from:bug fixesregressionsproduction incidentsarchitectural correctionsengineering reviewsThese become reusable engineering patterns.Knowledge Seeding PipelineGit History↓Architecture Documents↓Source Code↓Historical Documentation↓Capability Recovery↓Knowledge Normalization↓Knowledge Graph↓Engineer Agent↓Future ImplementationKnowledge must be normalized before entering the Knowledge Graph.Knowledge CategoriesKP organizes recovered knowledge into:ArchitectureCapabilitiesEngineering PatternsProduction PatternsImplementation PatternsRepository IntelligenceRuntime KnowledgeDeployment KnowledgeTransformation KnowledgeAI KnowledgeOperational KnowledgeLessons LearnedRegression PreventionEngineering DecisionsContinuous LearningKnowledge seeding is not a one-time activity.Every completed implementation executes the following cycle:Implementation↓Validation↓Knowledge Extraction↓Knowledge Review↓Knowledge Graph Update↓Engineer Agent Learning↓Improved Future EngineeringEvery production implementation must improve the Engineer Agent.Engineering RuleNo implementation begins until repository knowledge has been seeded.KP must learn from the past before building the future.The repository is the initial mentor for the Engineer Agent.Every subsequent implementation extends that knowledge through validated engineering experience.
I would also amend the roadmap itself to make Knowledge Seeding an explicit phase rather than part of KP.
The revised sequence becomes:


Foundation Layer


Universal Runtime


Repository Intelligence


Repository Knowledge Seeding (Git history, architecture, existing implementations, reconciliations, landing contract)


Knowledge Platform (Knowledge Graph + Engineer Agent)


AI Platform


Builder


Universal Transformation Engine (UTE)


Universal Deployment Engine (UDE)


Internal Engineering Platform


This ordering is more faithful to your architecture: KP cannot learn until there is knowledge to ingest, so seeding logically precedes the implementation of KP's learning behavior.
